title: Rumours
tagline: Say what was done to you, what happened to your annoyance, and what you heard.
hook: A rumour is going around school and everyone wants to tell Noa something. You'll need the passive for what was done to someone, the 'affected' passive for things that happened to you, and らしい for what you have heard.
goals: Show annoyance with the affected passive
Report what you heard with 〜らしい

points.title: 〜られる（passive）
points.formula: ru: stem + られる / u: あ-row + れる
points.gist: Say what was done to someone.
explain: Ru-verbs add られる: ほめる → ほめられる. U-verbs change the last sound to the あ-row and add れる: 選ぶ → 選ばれる, 読む → 読まれる, 書く → 書かれる. する → される, 来る → 来られる.
The person who is acted on becomes the subject, and the doer takes に: 先生に ほめられました (I was praised by the teacher).

examples.ja: ノアさんは|先生に|ほめられました。
examples.en: Noa was praised by the teacher.

examples.ja: ノアさんは|みんなに|選ばれました。
この|本は|世界中で|読まれて います。
examples.gloss: this|book (topic)|all over the world|is being read
examples.en: This book is read all over the world.

points.tip: Passive forms look like potential for ru-verbs: 食べられる, 見られる. Context decides.
points.watch: The doer is marked by に, not が. 先生が ほめられた is wrong.

points.title: 迷惑の受身（affected passive）
points.gist: Something happened to me and I did not like it.
explain: Japanese also uses the passive for things that happen to you and cause trouble, even with verbs that take no object in English: 雨に ふられました (I got rained on), 子どもに 泣かれました (my child cried on me).
Often the thing that was done also appears with を: おとうとに ケーキを 食べられました (my brother ate my cake). The feeling of annoyance is the point.

examples.ja: きのう、|雨に|ふられました。
examples.en: I got caught in the rain yesterday.

examples.ja: おとうとに|ケーキを|食べられました。
examples.en: My little brother ate my cake (and I'm annoyed).

examples.ja: 電車で|足を|ふまれました。
examples.en: My foot got stepped on in the train.

points.tip: Look for a hidden "…and I was bothered".
points.watch: Do not use it when the result is good. For good things use 〜てもらう.

points.title: 〜らしい
explain: Attach らしい to a plain-form sentence to say how things seem based on information you heard or saw: ノアさんが 選ばれたらしい. Nouns and な-adjectives drop だ: 休みらしい.
It tells the listener that this is not your own firsthand knowledge. Use 〜みたい or 〜ようだ when you have seen the evidence yourself.

examples.ja: あしたは|休みらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently tomorrow is a day off.

examples.ja: ハナさんは|かぜを|ひいたらしい。
examples.en: Apparently Hana has caught a cold.

points.tip: らしい = "I heard that, and it seems so".
points.watch: 〜らしい also means "typical of", as in 子どもらしい. Context tells you which.

drills.ja: ノアさんは 先生＿ ほめられました。
drills.en: Noa was praised by the teacher.

drills.q: What is the passive of 選ぶ?
Which is the passive of ほめる?

drills.ja: きのう、雨＿ ふられました。

drills.q: You got your foot stepped on:
options: 足を ふまれました。
足が ふまれました。
足に ふまれました。
drills.why: Affected passive keeps を for the thing.

drills.en: My little brother ate my cake.

drills.ja: あしたは 休み＿です。
drills.en: Apparently tomorrow is a day off.

drills.q: Which is "Apparently Hana caught a cold"?
options: ハナさんは かぜを ひいたらしい。
ハナさんは かぜを ひいたらしだ。
ハナさんは かぜを ひくらしくない。
ハナさんは かぜを ひいたのらしい。

drills.q: You heard from a friend that the cafe is closed:
options: あの 店は 休みらしいよ。
あの 店は 休みさせるよ。
あの 店は 休みられるよ。
あの 店は 休みなのらしいよ。
